easycreate.ponder.ender_tank_basics.head: Storing fluids in an Ender Fluid Tank
easycreate.ponder.ender_tank_basics.text: Ender Fluid Tanks store fluids just like Create's Fluid Tanks.
Use pipes and powered pumps to fill or drain the tank from any side.
Matching tanks can form larger tanks. Wireless transfer uses their shared fluid storage.
easycreate.ponder.ender_tank_wireless.te: Place a Redstone Link next to each Ender Fluid Tank, as with Ender Chutes.
Keep the first link in transmit mode. Sneak-right-click the other link to receive.
Set the same two frequency items in the same order on both links. Neither slot may be empty.
Fluid moves from sender to receiver, up to 1 bucket per tick per sending multiblock. No fluid is created.
A full tank or a different fluid stops transfer without losing the sender's fluid.
Both ends must be loaded in the same dimension. The Ender connection has no distance limit and does not load chunks.
easycreate.ponder.ender_controller_basic: Without a wireless link, the Ender controller works like Create's Rotation Speed Controller.
Place a Large Cogwheel above it, with its horizontal axis perpendicular to the controller's shaft.
Use the side value panel to set the target RPM. The connected cogwheel changes speed.
Negative RPM reverses rotation. A real power source and sufficient stress capacity are still required.
easycreate.ponder.ender_controller_wirel: Connect the transmitting controller to a real power source. The receiving shaft starts stopped.
Keep the first link in transmit mode. Sneak-right-click the other link to receive.
Set the same two frequency items in the same order on both links. Neither slot may be empty.
Matching links connect the two controllers. The receiving shaft now outputs rotation.
Adjust the receiver's target RPM. Its machines consume stress capacity from the sender's network.
Removing a link, changing its frequency or stopping the power source stops the receiver.
Like Ender Chutes, this works between loaded endpoints in one dimension, without a distance limit.
easycreate.ponder.ender_chute_basics.tex: Without a Redstone Link, an Ender Chute works like Create's Smart Chute.
Items enter from above and move into the inventory below.
Set a filter to select items. Use its value panel to choose the extraction amount.
Redstone power pauses the chute. Remove the signal to allow items through again.
easycreate.ponder.ender_chute_wireless.t: Put the source inventory above the sending chute and the destination below the receiving chute.
Keep the first link in transmit mode. Sneak-right-click the other link to receive.
Set the same two frequency items in the same order on both links. Neither slot may be empty.
Items move from the transmitter to the receiver. Each operation transfers at most 16 items.
Both filters must accept the item. The receiver's value panel sets the amount for each transfer.
Place an inventory below the receiver to collect items. Without one, items drop out below it.
Both ends must be loaded in the same dimension. There is no distance limit, and the chutes do not load chunks.
